name: King of Bela
overview: The King of Bela was a male ruler identified by his title as the king of the city of Bela, also known as Zoar, as mentioned in Genesis 14:2. There is no information provided about his tribal affiliation or additional personal notes. His unique attribute is his kingship over this specific location during the time recorded in Genesis.
namesAndTitles: This individual is known by the titles 'King of Bela' and 'King of Zoar,' which refer to the same city, Bela being another name for Zoar. No specific meanings of these titles are provided beyond their identification as royal titles mentioned in Genesis 14:2.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for the King of Bela beyond his designation as king. There are no listed relatives or connections to other biblical figures in the available data.
scriptureSignificance: The King of Bela is noted in the biblical narrative as a regional ruler during the period described in Genesis 14:2. His mention alongside other kings highlights the political landscape of the time and situates Bela (Zoar) within the broader context of the events recorded in Genesis. Although details about his actions or character are not provided, his role as king contributes to the historical setting of the passage.
